text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock has risen 9.6% over two weeks and gained 0.7% today as oil refineries operate near full capacity (96.8%) amid elevated global oil prices. The world crude price sits at $130.80 per barrel—nearly $24 above U.S. oil at $107—creating a wider price spread that generally benefits refiners, who buy crude and sell refined products like gasoline and diesel. Escalating tensions in the Middle East, including Houthi attacks, Iranian actions around the Strait of Hormuz, and incidents near Saudi Arabia's infrastructure, have sustained concerns about supply disruptions and kept crude prices elevated.

The sustained run-up since mid-September reflects the combination of tight refining capacity and geopolitical risk premiums on oil. With gasoline and diesel inventories relatively low (207.7 million and 107.9 million barrels respectively) and refiners running flat-out, the market appears to be pricing in continued strong demand for refined fuel and limited ability to expand output quickly if supplies tighten further.
